newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker after bond sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker after bond sell-off.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended weaker at C$1.3663 (US$0.7319) on Wednesday from Tuesday's close at C$1.3593 ($0.7356). Traders said weakness resulted from a sell-off on U.S. and Canadian fixed-income markets and comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that the Fed may need to raise interest rates before inflation gets worse.
Canadian bonds sank along with U.S. treasuries on Wednesday, with Canada's 30-year bond closing down C$1.50 to C$111.45 to yield 7.036 percent.
The Toronto Stock Exchange regained some of its early losses, but still finished the session down 46 points.
"Fears that the Fed would raise rates and the impact it would have on rate spreads probably weighed on (the Canadian dollar) today," another dealer said.
Traders said they expect the Canadian unit to range between C$1.3645 (US$0.7328) and C$1.3675 (US$0.7312) in overnight trading.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2361 marks from Tuesday's close at 1.2290 marks, but fell to 89.30 yen from Tuesday's close of 89.54 yen.
